Website · Quick start · Bug bounty · Verification · Documentation · Issues

 Pentest-AI is an open-source AI penetration testing and bug-bounty tool that keeps proven findings apart from guesses. It connects an AI client or model to a real pentest workflow: investigating web applications, discovering and reproducing vulnerabilities, and using machine oracles to verify whether an exploit actually works . A finding no oracle can prove stays labelled a candidate, and a verified one carries the requests and responses that proved it.

Use it through MCP (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, VS Code), from the CLI , or in CI/CD . The model drives the investigation; an independent oracle decides whether a finding earns a verified verdict, so the model's guesses never arrive dressed as results.

 Built for authorized bug bounty: one profile per program carries its scope, its stated rate and your researcher handle, a dry run shows the plan before anything is sent, and report drafts come from verified findings only. Jump to the bug-bounty workflow →

 Test only systems you own or have explicit authorization to assess. Read the acceptable-use policy and terms before running an engagement.

 Quick start

 Recommended: Codex or Claude Code

Use Python 3.10 to 3.14 and install pipx
first. Run pipx ensurepath and reopen your terminal if needed. pipx isolates
Pentest-AI's dependencies and makes its commands available across folders.

 

Install your AI client's CLI first. Setup asks before connecting all detected
supported clients , including both Codex and Claude Code when installed. It
preserves existing registrations. Restart your client afterward.

The wizard uses user-wide settings . It does not install clients, sign you in,
download models or configure Ollama. Your AI client supplies the model; no separate
model API key is required by the MCP server. Use ptai setup --mcp --dry-run to
preview changes. See single-client and per-repository setup
for Codex .codex/config.toml and Claude Code .mcp.json instructions.

For upgrades, use pipx upgrade ptai . In an existing activated virtual environment,
 python -m pip install --upgrade ptai is also supported; keep that environment
available after registering it with your AI client.

 Alternative: Ollama and local models

 Other model providers

For standalone cloud models and optional scanner dependencies, see the installation guide and provider guide. Keep API keys out of source control.

 Bug-bounty automation

Bug bounty mode is for programs that allow automated testing. You write one
profile per program with its scope, its stated rate and your researcher handle.
 --program then applies all of it to every request, and --dry-run prints the
plan without sending anything.

 

 

Under --program :

- Every request is held to the program's rate, external tools included. A tool
 that cannot be held to its share of the rate is skipped and the scan says so.
- Scope comes from the profile and nowhere else. Requests outside it are
 refused, and exclusions win over wildcards.
- Each request carries your researcher handle in X-Bug-Bounty , or in the
 header the program names ( PTAI BOUNTY HEADER NAME ). That includes requests
 from external tools and the browser. A tool that cannot carry the header is
 skipped.
- With no --scope , the scan runs the web phases. --scope full adds the
 Active Directory and cloud phases.
- ptai signs up no account on the target unless you pass --auto-auth . To scan
 with an account you made yourself, pass its session with --cookie ,
 --header or --basic-auth .
- Wordlist tools such as gobuster and ffuf are declined. Two built-in
 discovery probes still try a list of likely paths, about 500 requests.
- Payloads built to exhaust or crash the target are not sent. ptai does not log
 in as an account that is not yours, change records the scan did not create,
 place orders or move money. Race-condition bursts only run when the profile
 sets allow race = true . The guide lists what a scan still writes.
- The stored XSS probe does not run under a program, because it writes comments
 to pages other users read.
- 429 and Retry-After are honoured. A target that slows down gets a lower
 rate, and one that stays degraded stops the scan with the reason recorded.
- A program that bans scanners needs a typed yes , because scanning it can
 void safe harbour.

 ptai bounty-report drafts reports from oracle-verified findings only. The
steps come from what the finding recorded, and the draft includes the oracle's
request and response when its receipt holds them. Reproduce each one by hand
and submit it yourself. ptai bounty import converts a program's exported
scope file into allow and exclude entries for the profile.

Wall time is requests divided by rate. On our test application a full pass at
3 rps is about 8,700 requests and takes 51 minutes, and finds every critical
and high that a 10 rps pass finds. At 10 rps it was about 6,600 requests and 11
minutes, measured before slow probes got room to finish at low rates.

Counted at arrival, no second went over the declared rate at 3 or 10 rps,
including the requests sent by external tools.

install.html:
Recommended: Codex or Claude Code

Use Python 3.10 to 3.14 and install pipx first. Run pipx ensurepath and reopen your terminal if needed. pipx isolates Pentest-AI's dependencies and makes its commands available across folders.

pipx install ptai
ptai setup --mcp

Install your AI client's CLI first. Setup asks before connecting all detected supported clients, including both Codex and Claude Code when installed. It preserves existing registrations. Restart your client afterward.

The wizard uses user-wide settings. It does not install clients, sign you in, download models or configure Ollama. Your AI client supplies the model; no separate model API key is required by the MCP server. Use ptai setup --mcp --dry-run to preview changes. Alternative: Ollama and local models

Install Pentest-AI as above, but skip MCP setup for this route. Install and start Ollama, then pull a model with tool-calling support. Use ollama list to find its exact installed name.

export PENTEST_AI_LLM_PROVIDER=ollama
export PENTEST_AI_MODEL="your-installed-model"
ptai start https://your-authorized-target.example --no-sync

In PowerShell:

$env:PENTEST_AI_LLM_PROVIDER = "ollama"
$env:PENTEST_AI_MODEL = "your-installed-model"
ptai start https://your-authorized-target.example --no-sync

Replace the placeholders before running. A local model needs no cloud API key. Model quality and available memory affect results. See the model guide for endpoint configuration.

No API key or external target required.

pipx install ptai
ptai demo

The demo tests a bundled vulnerable application, replays a finding from its proof capsule, and checks the hardened routes. Inspect the evidence workflow before configuring a real engagement.
